consequences: Nothing the app does can change or lock e-Sword's files; new modules appear after a rescan; the app needs macOS permission to read another app's container, which is tied to the signature.
context: The app's content is the user's e-Sword X library, including licensed Bibles (NIV, ESV) that may not be redistributed, and new modules keep being downloaded in e-Sword.
decision: Open every module where e-Sword keeps it with SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY and immutable=1; never copy module files; rescan on demand; module files are gitignored.
title: Read e-Sword modules in place, read-only and immutable

consequences: Searches take about 0.5 s; first launch spends about 30 s indexing in the background; the index is derived and safe to delete.
context: LIKE over the commentaries and dictionaries reads several hundred MB per search, about 5 s even with SQLite optimised.
decision: Build an FTS5 contentless index in the app's data folder on a background thread, per module, keyed by file size and mtime; candidates from the index, exact phrase and whole-word rules applied in Rust; LIKE fallback while a module is unindexed or for part-word searches.
title: Full-text index for commentaries and dictionaries

consequences: Entries read naturally in Obsidian; edits there survive as long as the heading and comment stay; the editor only produces Markdown it can round-trip (headings, bold, italic, lists, quotes).
context: The user keeps notes in an Obsidian vault and wants the journal in a file they own.
decision: One YYYY-MM.md per month; each entry a '## Title' heading, a hidden tes comment with id, dates, verses and tags, a generated visible meta line, then the Markdown body; one paragraph per line, never hard-wrapped.
title: Journal as monthly Markdown files

consequences: Uses the user's existing sign-in; answers stream; no tools can run; licensed Bible text is sent only when Settings allows it.
context: The user wants AI answers without managing API keys, with a model choice.
decision: Run claude -p with stream-json output, partial messages, no tools and strict MCP config, in the app's data folder, appending a Bible-study system prompt; stream text deltas to the window as events; follow-ups resume the session; chats are stored locally.
title: Ask Claude through the local Claude Code CLI

consequences: Bible chats stay tool-free. A book chat stores its folder (bookDir) so resuming uses the same cwd and session. Changing the export layout needs books::VERSION bumped so old exports are redone.
context: Reference books run to ~170k words plus charts; sending a whole book with each question floods the context, and Bible chats deliberately run claude -p with no tools.
decision: Export the book once (books.rs) as index.txt, one text file per chapter and chart PNGs under the app's data dir; run book chats with cwd set to that folder, --tools Read,Grep,Glob and --permission-mode default, so reads outside the folder need a permission print mode refuses. Send the current chapter (or ~6,000 words around the paragraph asked about) with the question.
title: Ask about a book: read-only tools confined to an exported folder

consequences: Downloaded voices are selectable; the voice setting now stores the AVSpeechSynthesisVoice identifier (names still match). A local neural voice such as Kokoro would plug in behind the same commands. Non-macOS builds have no speech.
context: WKWebView's speechSynthesis.getVoices() lists only the voices that ship with macOS; Premium and Enhanced voices downloaded in System Settings never appear, though AVSpeechSynthesisVoice.speechVoices() returns them.
decision: src-tauri/src/tts.rs speaks through AVSpeechSynthesizer on the main thread; the page sends tts_speak/tts_stop with its generation number as the utterance id and gets word ranges and end-of-utterance back as 'tts' events. Rate is scaled as WebKit did (0.5 x page rate).
title: Read aloud through AVSpeechSynthesizer, not WebKit speechSynthesis

consequences: No commentary text is pasted into prompts any more; the '+ library' chip (settings.includeCommentaries) turns the folder on. Codex shows only its final message, since earlier ones are progress notes. Study folders untouched for 60 days are pruned at start.
context: Pasting two trimmed commentary excerpts into the prompt (single verse, first question only) left the model answering 'how do the commentators differ' from memory.
decision: src-tauri/src/study.rs writes a per-chat folder (<data>/ask/studies/<chat id>): the passage in every allowed Bible, every commentary entry overlapping the passage plus chapter/book introductions, and lexicon entries for its Strong's numbers; dictionaries are exported whole once (<data>/ask/dictionaries, redone when a module file changes) in the background at start and after a rescan. The chat runs in that folder with read-only search (Claude: Read/Grep/Glob plus --add-dir for dictionaries; Codex: read-only sandbox) and is told to answer from it and name sources.
title: Ask answers from the library by searching exported files

consequences: Codex answers arrive whole, not streamed. Codex's read-only sandbox can read outside a chat's folder; it is only told to stay inside. Claude chats keep their data/claude working folder so old sessions still resume; Codex uses data/codex.
context: Ask only ran the Claude Code CLI. Codex CLI can run non-interactively too (codex exec --json, resume by thread id), and the app should not show Ask when it cannot answer.
decision: src-tauri/src/assistant/ holds the shared prompt and process tracking, with claude.rs and codex.rs per CLI; a model id starting with 'claude' goes to Claude Code, anything else to Codex. Codex runs with --ignore-user-config --ignore-rules in the read-only sandbox, instructions passed as -c developer_instructions, and its models are read from the model cache Codex keeps in its home folder (entries with visibility=list). src/assistant.ts checks what is installed; with neither CLI every Ask control is hidden.
title: Ask supports Claude Code and Codex; hidden when neither is installed

consequences: Retake with make screenshots after any visual change. The Ask shot is a stored answer (tools/screenshots/ask-chat.json), regenerate it by hand if the answer format changes. Needs Screen Recording permission for the terminal.
context: Screenshots were taken by hand, one per screen, and went stale with every look change; macOS embedded the display's colour profile, which tinted them in browsers.
decision: tools/screenshots.py launches the dev build (cargo build --no-default-features, page from the Vite server) once per scene and theme with TES_SCENE set; src/scene.ts applies it (settings, screen, passage, a fixture chat, a still player) and api.ts stops all saving. The window is fixed at 1440x900, captured with screencapture -l by PID, resized to 1400 wide and saved without an ICC profile. Docs use <picture> with light and dark sources.
title: Screenshots are taken by a script, from scenes, in both themes

consequences: New ways of moving around should call these functions, not set screen or state directly, or back will skip them. DocReader filling in a book's chapter replaces the entry instead of pushing one.
context: Back and forward only recorded Bible passages, so they did nothing in Word Study, Search or between screens.
decision: state.tsx keeps a stack of places (screen, passage, open book chapter, Word Study target, search). Every navigation goes through navigate(): go, open, openDoc, closeDoc, studyWord, searchText, startEntry, setPending. Word Study's target may be an English word, so a lookup list is a place; Search runs a new query through searchText. back/forward restore a place without pushing.
title: One back/forward history of places for the whole app

consequences: New buttons and controls get a title as a matter of course. Disabled buttons show no tooltip (WebKit sends no pointer events to them). Tooltips are off in screenshot mode.
context: macOS's native tooltips look out of place beside the app's popovers; the app now has its own (Tooltips in src/ui.tsx), and a mix of the two looks broken.
decision: Every tooltip is the custom one. Give an element a title (or, for an icon-only button, an aria-label) and Tooltips shows it in the popover style, everywhere in the app. Do not build other tooltip components, and do not rely on native tooltips; keep title text short and useful (what it does, and its shortcut).
title: Always use the app's custom tooltip

consequences: About 8x faster (0.33 s). Totals can be a few percent higher than a strict text check, since the index also matches a phrase across punctuation; the library test allows that.
context: Searching a common word ("light", about 20,800 matches) took ~2.8 s in a release build, far longer in dev: every indexed match was loaded and converted to plain text just to be counted.
decision: For an indexed whole-word search, candidate_rows counts the index's matches in SQL (with the book-range filter) and loads only the rows shown (limit + 10), which are still text-checked for their snippets.
title: Search counts come from the index, not a text check of every match

consequences: A book renamed in its module breaks its labels' links. Notes on a chapter are found by matching the book's title and chapter title.
context: Paragraphs of reference books and devotionals needed the verse tools (highlight, bookmark, note, listen, ask, copy) and a study pane, but journal entries link verses by readable strings and highlights are keyed by book.chapter.verse.
decision: src/docref.ts: a journal entry links a paragraph by the label 'Book title › Chapter ¶n' (or ¶n–m, or no ¶ for the chapter) in its verses list, so the Markdown stays readable; highlights use the key doc|module|title|para in the same store; bookmarks carry a DocSpot. DocReader selects paragraphs on click (not on a word), shows the verse toolbar as icons, and has a study pane with Notes, Dictionary and Ask (settings.docTab).
title: Book paragraphs are linked, highlighted and bookmarked like verses

consequences: No reminder once the app is quit. Clicking the notification does not start Quiet time; the menu's Start Quiet Time item does.
context: The window hides rather than closes and a hidden WKWebView throttles timers, so a JS timer can't be trusted to fire at the reminder time.
decision: src/tray.tsx sends a TrayState (today's reading, done, place, reminder on and time) via set_tray once saved settings and plans have loaded; src-tauri/src/tray.rs rebuilds the menu-bar menu from it and a thread checks every 30s, firing a notification within 2h after the time, at most once a day (last fired date kept in the store as reminder.json). Menu choices come back to the page as 'tray' events.
title: Quiet time reminder is timed in Rust, not the page

consequences: Needs the apple-events entitlement and NSAppleEventsUsageDescription (src-tauri/Entitlements.plist, Info.plist); the first use prompts for Automation permission. Catalogue songs not in the library can't be chosen. Choosing takes 15-35s with ~1500 candidates, so it starts when the session starts and a day's choice is cached in memory.
context: Worship songs for Quiet time should suit the day's reading. Apple Music catalogue playback needs MusicKit and a paid developer token; the Music app's library can be driven by osascript with no account setup.
decision: List the library's Christian/gospel/worship-genre songs via JXA, have the assistant choose by number from that numbered list (so it can only name songs that exist), queue them in the app's own playlist 'Two-edged Sword · Quiet time' (deleted and remade each time, never touching other playlists) and play it. Pause/skip only act while that playlist is playing. Random choice when no assistant or the answer can't be parsed.
title: Quiet time worship songs come from the Music library, picked by number

consequences: Chats from before this change whose index points at the shared dictionaries folder can no longer read dictionaries. The user's own Claude Code settings still load and could widen what it reads; documented, not closed.
context: The Licensed translations switch only swapped the Bible used for the passage; licensed commentaries, lexicons and dictionaries still went into the chat folder, Compare and Search sent licensed verses, and book chats sent licensed books. Dictionaries were shared via --add-dir, so any of them could be read.
decision: Renamed to Licensed text. When off, isLicensed modules of every kind are withheld: Bibles fall back to public-domain text or send the reference only; study export takes an exclude list; dictionaries are hard-linked per chat so only allowed ones are reachable and --add-dir is gone; Compare, Search and book chats send no licensed text.
title: Licensed text off withholds every licensed module from Ask, not just Bibles

consequences: A refused action ends agy's turn with no answer; the app reports that as an error. The user's own Antigravity rules files still load, and agy keeps its own history in its own history folder in the home directory. If agy stops enforcing agent tool lists, web search returns silently.
context: Gemini CLI was retired for personal accounts in June 2026 in favour of Antigravity CLI (agy). agy has no flag to limit tools, uses web search unprompted (search_web is not a permission action, so settings can't deny it), and its project settings file wasn't honoured in print mode.
decision: Each run writes .agents/agents/tes-ask.md into its working folder: a mainAgent with inheritMcp false and tools limited to view_file, grep_search, find_by_name, list_dir (or [] outside a folder chat), and runs agy -p --agent tes-ask --sandbox. Tested: the tools list is enforced (the model reports no web search tool); reads outside the folder, commands and read_url are refused in print mode. Model ids are prefixed agy: since it also offers Claude models.
title: Antigravity CLI for Ask, confined by a per-run custom agent

consequences: An organisation's Copilot policy can block the CLI (seen on this account at first). Instructions in the user turn are weaker than a system prompt. No model choice beyond Auto.
context: copilot -p has --available-tools, --disable-builtin-mcps and --no-custom-instructions, but no system-prompt flag and no way to list models (not in -p, errors or ACP session/new).
decision: Folder chats get --available-tools=view,grep,glob; others get view only in an empty working folder, because an empty --available-tools= means every tool (it tried web_fetch in testing). Ask's instructions open the first message; follow-ups resume with --resume. One model, copilot:auto.
title: GitHub Copilot CLI for Ask: --available-tools, instructions in the first message, Auto only

consequences: An external edit that keeps both size and mtime (rare) would be missed until the next change. Sync tools that go by mtime rather than file events could skip an upload; OneDrive's File Provider sees the rename.
context: The user wants editing an entry not to change its month file's mtime (they also asked this of bulk retagging); an old month shouldn't look new to Finder, Obsidian's sort or backups.
decision: write_month reads the file's mtime before the atomic write and sets it back afterwards; a new month file keeps its creation time. Change detection is unaffected: stamp() also compares sizes, the app reloads after its own saves, and other editors change the mtime themselves.
title: Journal saves keep the month file's modified time

consequences: A misspelling that happens to be a KJV word isn't caught. Without a KJV module nothing changes. The set isn't rebuilt on Rescan.
context: The journal's macOS spell checker flagged KJV spellings (maketh, remaineth, names) and the grammar checker flagged KJV English (he maketh me, thou art); the user had been adding KJV words to the shared macOS dictionary one by one.
decision: At start a background thread reads every word of the library's KJV (a Bible with abbreviation KJV, tags stripped) into a set (about 12.8k words); spell::check drops flagged words in it. A sentence with grammar issues is skipped when it has a marker (thee, thou, hath, unto…) or a KJV word macOS flags. A check that comes before the read has finished does the read itself, since the editor caches results per paragraph. The user's learned KJV words were unlearned (16).
title: The KJV's words count as spelled right in the journal

consequences: The journal stays the user's own. A new translation is one candidates run, one review and one build. The file is not in the repo, so it is rebuilt from the work folder if lost.
context: Wayne wanted every place the NIV departs in meaning from the KJV flagged, and the same for other translations later. There are hundreds per translation.
decision: tools/variances/ finds candidates by script, agents review them against review.md, and build.py writes variances-<module>.json to the app data folder. The reading pane shows a marker in Verse layout from that file. Records hold only the reference, category, a short change and a note: never the translation's text, which is read from the module.
title: Translation variances live in a per-module data file, not the journal

consequences: About 5% of words, where SEDRA's text differs from the 1905 Bible Society text, are left without a gloss; glosses are dictionary senses, with a COMMON table overriding SEDRA for the commonest little words; the tokenizer counts Syriac as an original language
context: The Peshitta has no Strong's numbers (Syriac has none); ETCBC's syrnt (MIT, from SEDRA 3) tags every NT word, and SEDRA IV's API has English glosses, but SEDRA calls itself non-commercial and its site says all rights reserved
decision: tools/syriac/build.py lines syrnt's words up with peshitta.bbli per chapter, takes glosses from SEDRA's API (cached), and writes peshitta+.bbli in INT+'s <div> markup; the module is built on the user's machine only
title: Peshitta+ is built locally from syrnt and SEDRA, never committed

consequences: About 2% of words have no English; glosses are dictionary senses and some tags are wrong; the builder needs a ~1 GB venv; tokenize's <div> path now takes the box's word in any script
context: No Vulgate with per-word English exists; Open Words (Python Whitaker) failed common words (creavit) and picked absurd senses (caelum: beer)
decision: tools/latin tags each verse with Stanza's PROIEL Latin model (in-context lemma and grammar) in a cached venv, and takes the most frequent Whitaker DICTLINE entry's first sense for the lemma, with a MEANINGS table for Biblical senses and case-aware personal pronouns; -que is split off as and
title: Latin+ Bibles are tagged by Stanza and glossed from Whitaker

consequences: About 39% of Onkelos/Jonathan words and 34% of Ps-Jon's are paired; 9-12% have no English; Jastrow glosses are often off; the tooltip says Hebrew or Jastrow so a reader can tell
context: No lemmatised Targum with English is freely available (CAL isn't downloadable); Jastrow is, but its first gloss is often a homograph's
decision: tools/targum pairs each Targum word with a cognate word of the same verse in WLC+ (consonants, prefixes and endings set aside, Aramaic-Hebrew letter correspondences, an order-keeping best pairing, EQUIV for non-cognates like יי for יהוה/אלהים) and takes its English and Strong's number; unpaired words take COMMON (the ~250 commonest) or Jastrow's first gloss after stripping affixes, preferring Aramaic (ch.) entries
title: Targum+ glosses come from pairing with WLC+, then a table, then Jastrow
